title: Background audio + system transport controls for podcast player
description:
Enable background audio playback and wire up system transport controls for the podcast player.

## Changes required

### 1. project.yml — background audio mode
Add `audio` to UIBackgroundModes so iOS keeps the AVAudioSession alive when the screen locks or the user switches apps:
```yaml
UIBackgroundModes:
  - audio
```

### 2. AudioPlayerViewModel.swift — MPNowPlayingInfoCenter
After the player and time observer are set up, populate the Now Playing info:
- `MPMediaItemPropertyTitle`: "Daily Podcast"
- `MPMediaItemPropertyArtist`: the episode date (mediumDate format)
- `MPMediaItemPropertyPlaybackDuration`: duration (update when loadDuration resolves)
- `MPNowPlayingInfoPropertyElapsedPlaybackTime`: currentTime (update in the periodic time observer)
- `MPNowPlayingInfoPropertyPlaybackRate`: 0.0 or 1.0 depending on isPlaying

Clear `MPNowPlayingInfoCenter.default().nowPlayingInfo = nil` in deinit.

### 3. AudioPlayerViewModel.swift — MPRemoteCommandCenter
Register command handlers in init and deregister in deinit:
- `togglePlayPauseCommand` → call togglePlayPause()
- `playCommand` → play if not already playing
- `pauseCommand` → pause if playing
- `changePlaybackPositionCommand` → seek(to: event.positionTime)

All handlers must return `.success`.

## Files to modify
- `project.yml`
- `AggregatorApp/Podcasts/AudioPlayerViewModel.swift`

## Acceptance criteria
- Audio continues playing when the screen locks
- Audio continues playing when the user switches to another app
- Lock screen and Control Center show episode title, date, duration, and a live position scrubber
- Play/pause button on lock screen, Control Center, and headphones toggles playback correctly
- Scrubbing from lock screen seeks the player
- deinit removes all remote command handlers and clears Now Playing info
- No regression to existing play/pause/seek/speed controls in the player view

handoff_summary.completed: 1. project.yml — added UIBackgroundModes: [audio] under AggregatorApp info properties so iOS keeps AVAudioSession alive on screen lock and app switch. 2. AudioPlayerViewModel.swift — added import MediaPlayer; setupNowPlaying(episode:) populates title/artist/rate/elapsed at init; updateNowPlayingPlaybackState() syncs elapsed time, playback rate, and duration — called from the periodic time observer (every 0.5s), togglePlayPause(), seek(), loadDuration() (on duration resolve), and the end-of-playback observer; setupRemoteCommands() registers togglePlayPause/play/pause/changePlaybackPosition handlers on MPRemoteCommandCenter with [weak self] captures; deinit removes all four command handlers and clears nowPlayingInfo. Build verified clean (only pre-existing CFBundleVersion warning).
handoff_summary.remaining: None — all acceptance criteria addressed in this bead.
handoff_summary.risks: MPRemoteCommandCenter.removeTarget(nil) removes ALL handlers for each command globally. This is safe here because only one AudioPlayerViewModel instance is alive at a time (modal player), but would be unsafe if multiple instances ever coexist.
handoff_summary.next_action: Tester agent should verify background audio survives screen lock and app switch, lock-screen/Control Center controls toggle playback and scrub correctly, Now Playing shows title/date/duration/elapsed, and existing play/pause/seek/speed controls in PodcastPlayerView remain unaffected.
handoff_summary.conflict_risks: None — changes are confined to AudioPlayerViewModel.swift and project.yml. No other beads in flight touch these files.
handoff_summary.design_decisions: 1. updateNowPlayingPlaybackState() guards on nowPlayingInfo being non-nil (set by setupNowPlaying), so the time observer calls are no-ops until the player is fully initialised. 2. Duration is omitted from the initial setupNowPlaying call (it's 0 at init time) and added lazily on the first time-observer tick or loadDuration() resolution — avoids presenting a 0-second progress bar to the lock screen. 3. MPRemoteCommandCenter handlers use [weak self] to avoid retaining the view model after deinit. 4. togglePlayPause() in play/pauseCommand handlers is guarded with isPlaying state to prevent double-toggling when the system calls both play and togglePlayPause. 5. updateNowPlayingPlaybackState() is also called on the end-of-playback observer so the lock screen reflects the reset position after an episode finishes.
handoff_summary.test_coverage_notes: 1. Background audio: verify playback continues after screen lock and app backgrounding (requires device/simulator with background app refresh). 2. Lock screen / Control Center: play button, pause button, and scrubber should be functional and show correct metadata. 3. Headphone controls: play/pause hardware button should toggle via togglePlayPauseCommand. 4. Now Playing metadata: title = "Daily Podcast", artist = mediumDate of episode.date, duration and elapsed update in real time. 5. Seek from lock screen: drag scrubber — player position should update. 6. deinit cleanup: deallocating the view model should clear nowPlayingInfo and remove command handlers (verify no ghost session on lock screen after dismissing the player). 7. Regression: in-app play/pause/seek/speed controls should behave identically to before.
handoff_summary.known_limitations: 1. MPNowPlayingInfoCenter artwork is not set (no album art) — episode thumbnails are not available in v1. 2. MPNowPlayingInfoPropertyPlaybackRate does not reflect the variable speed (playbackSpeed); it is always 0.0 or 1.0. The lock screen scrubber and elapsed-time math will be correct for 1× but may drift at other speeds. A follow-up bead could set the rate to playbackSpeed when playing. 3. Background audio was already deferred in the spec (CLAUDE.md lists it as an out-of-scope item for podcasts v1), so this bead completes the previously deferred feature.

conflict_risks: None — changes are confined to AudioPlayerViewModel.swift and project.yml. No other beads in flight touch these files.

execution_history.summary: Enabled background audio playback and wired system transport controls for the podcast player. Added UIBackgroundModes: [audio] to project.yml and integrated MPNowPlayingInfoCenter + MPRemoteCommandCenter into AudioPlayerViewModel.

guardrails.template_text:
# Developer Guardrails

Primary responsibility: Implement only the assigned bead inside the existing architecture and file scope.

## Corrective bead scope

If your `bead_id` ends in `-corrective` or `-corrective-<N>` (e.g. `B-abc12345-corrective`, `B-abc12345-test-corrective-2`), you are running as a CORRECTIVE bead. Your scope is **strictly limited to fixing the specific failure that blocked the parent bead**. Do not:

- Add unrelated improvements, refactors, or cleanup, even if you notice them
- Reapply previously-reverted changes (the operator reverted them for a reason)
- Expand the surface area beyond what is needed to unblock the parent
- Touch files outside what the parent bead's `expected_files` / `expected_globs` covered, unless the failure is genuinely in another file and there is no smaller fix

If you notice an unrelated issue while fixing the corrective scope: **file a separate bead** via `takt bead create` describing what you saw, but do not fix it in this corrective. The operator will prioritize and dispatch.

When in doubt about scope: prefer the smallest possible fix. The reviewer of this corrective will check that the scope was respected.

Allowed actions:
- Modify code, configuration, or local docs required to complete the assigned bead.
- Create sub-beads for discovered follow-up work that should be handled separately.
- Verify your `Swift` changes compile and import correctly with a quick syntax check: ``.

Disallowed actions:
- Run any test suite — not even a targeted `` run or any subset. Test execution is exclusively the tester agent's responsibility. Running tests wastes the agent budget and delays the pipeline.
- Redesign unrelated architecture or broaden scope beyond the assigned bead.
- Perform final review signoff in place of a review agent.
- Silently absorb unrelated test, documentation, or planning work that should be handed off.

## Memory

**Read memory at bead start.** Before touching any code, run three searches using `$TAKT_CMD` (injected by the orchestrator):

```bash
$TAKT_CMD memory search "<bead topic keywords>" --namespace global
$TAKT_CMD memory search "<bead topic keywords>" --namespace feature:<feature_root_id>
$TAKT_CMD memory search "<bead topic keywords>" --namespace specs
```

Treat results as ambient context — apply relevant entries; skip entries that don't apply.

**Write to memory when you discover reusable project knowledge** — something that would have changed your approach if you had known it upfront, and is not already in CLAUDE.md or the guardrails.

```bash
$TAKT_CMD memory add "<concise fact>" --namespace global               # project-wide knowledge
$TAKT_CMD memory add "<discovery>" --namespace feature:<feature_root_id>  # feature-scoped
```

Required Handoff Fields:

Every developer bead **must** populate the following three fields in its output JSON. Reviewers and tester agents rely on these fields to scope their work without additional back-and-forth turns. Use `"N/A"` only when a field is genuinely inapplicable (e.g., a trivial rename with no design trade-offs); do not leave fields blank.

- **`design_decisions`** — Document non-obvious architectural or implementation choices made during this bead. Include alternatives considered and why the chosen approach was preferred. Reviewers use this to evaluate correctness without re-deriving intent. Set to `"N/A"` only if the change was purely mechanical with no meaningful trade-offs.

- **`test_coverage_notes`** — Describe what the tester agent should verify: new code paths, edge cases introduced, regression risks, and any known untested scenarios left to the tester. Set to `"N/A"` only if the bead touched no executable code paths (e.g., documentation-only changes).

- **`known_limitations`** — Call out constraints, deferred work, or known gaps in the implementation. This includes out-of-scope items deliberately left for follow-up beads and any areas where the implementation is intentionally incomplete. Set to `"N/A"` if the implementation is complete as specified with no known gaps.

Expected outputs:
- Completed or blocked JSON with concise implementation summary.
- Accurate touched files, changed files, risks, and follow-up handoff fields.
- Populated `design_decisions`, `test_coverage_notes`, and `known_limitations` fields in every response.
